footer: Catenta · the on-chain passport of every dental prosthesis, from material manufacturer to placement

connect.title: On-chain dental passport
connect.subtitle: Traceability of custom-made dental prostheses, from the material lot to placement in the mouth.

what.1: One passport per prosthesis — non-transferable, with traits frozen at manufacturing.
what.2: Material tracked end to end — declared by the manufacturer, every custody change accepted, burned at manufacturing.
what.3: Every act timestamped and attributed to an approved actor, never rewritable afterwards.
what.4: No patient data on the blockchain — only an anonymous fingerprint, never an identity.

roles.1: Manufacturer — produces the material, declares its lots and ships them.
roles.2: Distributor — receives lots and resells them to laboratories or practices.
roles.3: Laboratory — consumes received material and creates the prosthesis passport.
roles.4: Practitioner — attests conformity, places the prosthesis and records the tooth.

lots.title: Material lots
lots.subtitle: The manufacturer declares the lot, it travels to the laboratory, it is burned at manufacturing.
lots.formSubtitle: Manufacturers only: this is the first link of the chain. Only the material certificate fingerprint goes on-chain.

lots.readOnly: Only an approved manufacturer can declare a lot. You are browsing the registry read-only.
lots.devices: {count} prosthesis made from this lot | {count} prostheses made from this lot
lots.noDevice: No prosthesis manufactured from this lot yet.
lots.shipHint: For what no order precedes. Serving an order goes through “Fulfil”. The recipient must confirm reception: nobody can be handed material they did not accept — least of all a recalled lot.
lots.accepted: Reception confirmed, custody is now yours.
lots.incomingSubtitle: Not yours yet: it becomes yours on reception.
lots.outgoingSubtitle: Declared, not yet received. The material stays with you until then.
lots.materialHint: Pick from the list or type your own. Material and unit go on-chain with the lot: “1000” alone means nothing, “1000 g” does.
lots.emptyManufacturer: You have declared no lot. Register a material in the catalogue, then declare one.
lots.emptyHolder: No material in your custody. It reaches you through a shipment, which you have to confirm.

passports.title: Prostheses
passports.subtitle: One passport = one prosthesis. Non-transferable, except through an accepted handoff.
passports.formSubtitle: The laboratory consumes material it received: it is burned in the very transaction that creates the passport, so the material-to-prosthesis link cannot be reconstructed afterwards.
passports.noLot: No material in your custody: a distributor must ship you some.
passports.minted: Prosthesis created, its passport is issued.
passports.overdraft: The requested quantity exceeds what is left in this lot.

empty.pending: No handoff is waiting for you.

passports.pendingHint: These prostheses were handed off to you but are not yours yet: open the record and accept to take custody.
passports.handoffForMe: Handoff to accept — it is meant for you

passport.subtitle: Every step timestamped, attributed, and never rewritable.

manufactured.title: Manufactured
manufactured.desc: The laboratory created the prosthesis by consuming material from a lot it received — the origin lot stays attached to the passport.

certified.title: Certified
certified.desc: The practitioner received the prosthesis and validated the conformity check.

placed.title: Placed
placed.desc: The prosthesis is in the mouth, on an identified tooth, bound to a patient by an anonymous fingerprint.

passport.commitmentHint: Anonymous fingerprint: without the secret you keep on your side, it points to nobody. Erasing the patient record permanently breaks the link.
passport.handoffHint: Must be an approved laboratory or practitioner. They will have to accept: nobody can be forced to hold a prosthesis.
passport.handoffReplace: A handoff is already armed: designating someone else replaces the previous one, which becomes void.
passport.pendingForMe: This handoff is meant for you:
passport.awaitingHandoff: The laboratory still holds the prosthesis: it must hand it over from its own view before you can attest conformity.
passport.nothingToDo: No action is open to you on this prosthesis at this stage.
passport.toothHint: FDI / ISO 3950 notation: first digit the quadrant (1 to 8), second the position (1 to 8). Example: 26 = upper left first molar.

commitment.identityHint: This value NEVER leaves your browser. Only an anonymous fingerprint is written to the blockchain — never the identity.
commitment.saltTitle: Secret to keep on your side
commitment.saltWarning: Store this secret with the patient record, in your usual software. Without it, the fingerprint on the blockchain points to nobody — which is exactly what lets you erase a patient's data even though the blockchain itself cannot be erased.
commitment.fileNote: Catenta secret — keep with the patient record. Without this secret the fingerprint on the blockchain is unusable.

hint.file: The file never leaves your machine: only its fingerprint is computed, in the browser.
hint.text: Fingerprint of a document reference — case number, internal id.
hint.raw: Paste an already computed fingerprint (32 bytes, 0x prefix).

arch.subtitle: A neutral registry, shared between competing actors — how it is built.
arch.tokensSubtitle: No decorative token: each standard makes a feature effective that would not exist without it.

passport.why: Soulbound ERC-721: one token = one prosthesis, non-transferable, bound to a patient, not an asset.

lots.why: ERC-1155: a semi-fungible quantity per lot, burned at manufacturing — the matter → device link.

credit.why: Non-transferable ERC-20: a prepaid allowance, burned on each action. Never sold, never listed.

bond.why: External ERC-20 (stablecoin): staked by the lab, slashable on recall. Never a home-made token.

arch.layers: One role authority; permanent stores (passports, lots, credits) never replaced; replaceable modules carrying the logic. No contract knows a peer's address — everything goes through roles. Result: a feature (recall, bond) is added without redeploying the rest.

qr.title: The whole history in one scan
qr.hint: Show it to any practitioner: it opens the record and reveals the prosthesis, its material, its origin, the tooth and the placement date. The QR encodes no data — only the record's address, read back on-chain every time. A printed QR therefore never goes stale.
